clusters.name: Identity and Credential Security
clusters.description: Authentication mechanisms and credential-protection choices, distinguished from session termination and domain workflow behavior.

relations.rationale: Credential authentication and protection determine which secure identity context can be established for CityBike sessions.
Authenticated identity is required before protected rental operations such as QR-based unlocking can begin.

values.label: Email/password authentication
values.description: Uses email and password as the primary user authentication mechanism.

values.label: Transport and storage protection
values.description: Protects credentials during transmission and while stored by the platform.

values.label: Ephemeral verification codes
values.description: Uses short-lived verification codes to reduce replay and unauthorized account-verification risk.

clusters.name: Session Lifecycle Control
clusters.description: Session lifecycle policies governing how authenticated access is ended, independently of credential validation or rental state.

relations.rationale: Session termination operationalizes the security boundary established by identity and credential mechanisms.

values.label: Immediate logout termination
values.description: Provides an explicit logout action that immediately invalidates or ends the current user session.

clusters.name: Rental Workflow State Management
clusters.description: State and interaction models for progressing users and rentals through unlock, active-use, and return stages.

relations.rationale: Rental workflows require authenticated users before unlocking or changing protected rental states.
Reliable rental state tracking generally requires persistence for current lifecycle state and historical usage data.
State transitions create the changes that clients and operational components need to receive in real time.
Command objects provide an implementation form for actions represented by the rental workflow.

values.label: State-machine workflow
values.description: Represents navigation and rental progression with explicit states rather than ad hoc conditional transitions.

values.label: QR-based bike unlocking
values.description: Starts a rental by scanning a bike QR code and transitioning the rental into an unlocked state.

values.label: Rental lifecycle state tracking
values.description: Tracks checkout, active ride, return, and related bike-status transitions as explicit lifecycle states.

clusters.name: Persistence and Data Access
clusters.description: Abstractions and policies for storing, querying, and retrieving operational and analytical CityBike data.

relations.rationale: Rental lifecycle and bike status decisions depend on a way to persist and query domain state.

values.label: Repository-based persistence abstraction
values.description: Uses repositories to decouple domain services from persistence technology while supporting bike-data queries.

values.label: Usage-statistics persistence
values.description: Persists and retrieves usage statistics alongside operational bike information for platform analysis.

clusters.name: Real-Time Notification Delivery
clusters.description: Mechanisms for propagating state changes to user interfaces or components, emphasizing timing and delivery behavior.

relations.rationale: Rental and bike-state transitions are the source events that notifications communicate to clients and dependent components.
Event-driven processing can deliver asynchronous updates that become user-visible or operational notifications.

values.label: Observer-based state notifications
values.description: Uses observers to push rental-state changes to the UI or subscribed components.

values.label: Scheduled event delivery
values.description: Uses scheduler assistance when notification dispatch requires deferred or timed delivery.

values.label: UI synchronization on state change
values.description: Updates client components when rental state changes so displayed availability and ride status remain synchronized.

clusters.name: Bike Lifecycle Event Integration
clusters.description: Asynchronous propagation of bike registration, update, and removal events across services or processing components.

relations.rationale: Asynchronous bike lifecycle events can produce downstream state updates that notification mechanisms expose to users or operators.
Event-driven processing and command-based operations are complementary but distinct interaction styles for service coordination.

values.label: Event-driven bike registration
values.description: Treats bike registration as an initiating domain event that triggers subsequent processing.

values.label: Asynchronous downstream bike updates
values.description: Processes bike removal and update actions asynchronously after the registration event.

clusters.name: Rental Operation Command Strategy
clusters.description: Encapsulation and applicability boundaries for executing rental actions, separate from notification scheduling and event delivery.

relations.rationale: Command encapsulation organizes actions performed within the rental workflow but does not determine workflow states themselves.
Explicitly excluding commands from notification scheduling preserves a separate event-delivery mechanism for asynchronous updates.

values.label: Command-based rental operations
values.description: Encapsulates rental operations as command objects to separate action requests from their execution.

values.label: Separate notification scheduling
values.description: Keeps notification scheduling outside the Command pattern, assigning it to a distinct delivery approach.

saturation_history.rationale: All relevant open codes are already subsumed by the existing taxonomy. The navigation state machine and QR-based bike unlock flow fall under Rental Workflow State Management; real-time bike status updates are captured by Real-Time Notification Delivery and its UI synchronization/observer variants; email/password authentication, secure transmission, and secure storage are covered by Identity and Credential Security; immediate session termination is covered by Session Lifecycle Control; repository-based persistence, bike data querying, and usage statistics persistence fit Persistence and Data Access; event-driven registration and asynchronous downstream updates are covered by Bike Lifecycle Event Integration; and the command-pattern codes are covered by Rental Operation Command Strategy. No open code introduces a genuinely new architectural axis for the CityBike use case.

All relevant open codes are already subsumed by the existing taxonomy. Rental duration tracking, pre-timeout expiry notification, scheduler-driven timing notifications, and bike status change/UI update codes fit within Rental Workflow Management and Event and Notification Propagation. Verification code generation, delivery, 30-minute validity, and secure authentication support are covered by Identity and Credential Security, including ephemeral verification-code authentication and token validity. Downloadable usage history report generation and Builder-based assembly are covered by Data Access and Reporting. Payment facade abstraction and delegation to underlying payment services are covered by Payment Integration Strategy. The remaining codes (state pattern for rental lifecycle, observer-based notifications, bike availability refresh, and related UI/model updates) are already represented in the taxonomy’s workflow, event propagation, and encapsulation dimensions. No genuinely new architectural concern is introduced by this minibatch relative to the CityBike use case.
